body:
Can monkeys be friends with horses? How about
giraffes and goats? It seems that animals of
different species are not ⓐcompatible with one
another, but there is one special friendship that
bloomed between a dog and a dolphin. The close
friendship between Gunner, a seven-year-old dog,
and Delta, a ten-year-old dolphin, is an extraordinary bond that goes beyond the
boundaries of their species. Despite their differences
in habitat, Gunner and Delta have formed a deep
and genuine connection that shows the beauty of
friendship between different species. Their first
encounter occurred when Gunner’s owner took him
to the Dolphin Research Center where Delta lives.
As Gunner ⓑobserved Delta swimming elegantly in
the water, he could not help but be fascinated by
the dolphin’s grace and friendliness. Gunner, with
his playful and ⓒloyal nature, seemed to be initially
intrigued by Delta’s graceful movements and
intelligent behavior. Gunner approached the edge of
the ⓓenclosure and walked alongside the water
while wagging his tail, his tongue hanging out in
excitement. Delta, being an exceptionally clever
creature, sensed Gunner’s friendly intentions and
politely swam over to meet him. The two animals
ⓔinspected each other with cautious sniffs and
gentle touches, quickly establishing a sense of trust.
Their friendship blossomed through shared
playfulness and mutual respect. Gunner and Delta
would have fun together, engaging in playful
games. For example, Gunner would bounce around
and
chase
Delta’s splashes,
and Delta would perform leaps for Gunner’s amusement. Their
interactions were a harmonious dance of joy and
companionship, (A)_____________________________________
_________________________________________________________.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ compatible: capable of existing together inharmony
ⓑ observe: to obey a rule, law, or custom
ⓒloyal: always supporting someone or somethingand being faithful to them
ⓓ enclosure: an area surrounded by a wall orfence and used for a particularpurpose
ⓔ inspect: to examine something carefully inorder to find out more about it
solution: ⓑ observe는 본문에서 ‘~을 목격하다’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나, ‘to obey a rule, law, or custom(규칙, 법, 또는 관습에 따르다)’는 observe의 또 다른 뜻인 ‘~을 준수하다’에 대한 영영풀이이므로, ‘to watch someone or something carefully(’누군가 또는 어떤 것을 주의 깊게 지켜보다)‘와 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Picasso’s visits to Arias’s barbershop became somewhat routine after that. Whenever he visited, the other customers let him be served first. This situation made Picasso feel uncomfortable because it caused other people to wait longer. Sensing his (A)[discomfort / disappointment], Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to get haircuts and shaves at home. Picasso happily accepted the offer. Arias went to Picasso’s house to cut his hair from then on, but he (B)[always / never] charged Picasso for his services. In return, Picasso gave him sketches, paintings, and ceramics as a gesture of friendship. As their friendship grew (C)[weaker / stronger], Arias started to drop by Picasso’s house, not to shave or cut his hair, but to hang out. Picasso once said to Arias, “You are always welcome to come to my house. When you’re here, I feel like I’m back in Spain.” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared by Arias’s mother. When they dined together, they would sit and talk for hours.
choices: discomfort – never – weaker
disappointment – always – weaker
disappointment – never – stronger
discomfort – always – stronger
discomfort – never – stronger
solution:
1. (A) 다른 손님들이 자기 때문에 더 오래 기다려 피카소가 불편해했으므로 discomfort(불편함)가 알맞다.
2. (B) 그 보답으로 피카소가 스케치·그림·도자기를 주었으므로 아리아스는 요금을 전혀 받지 않았다(never).
3. (C) 이발이 아니라 함께 시간을 보내러 들르고 몇 시간씩 이야기했으므로 우정이 더 강해졌다(stronger).
따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
One day, Picasso was busy painting War and
Peace, one of his largest projects, when Arias paid
him a visit. Picasso had been working hard staying
up at night for days.
(A) A few years later, Arias returned to Spain and
exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit
attracted visitors from all over the world. A
foreign merchant approached Arias one day and
attempted to persuade him to sell all of
Picasso’s works. But he refused to ㉠[exhibit /
bargain], saying, “Even if ⓐyou bring all the
money in your country, I will not sell any of his
works to you. His works are symbols of the
friendship between Picasso and me.”
(B) Arias responded that he would build a museum
in Spain to display the works. Picasso was
㉡[moved / confused] to hear that and swore to
help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to
see the museum completed, passing away in
1973. Arias was in grief and despair but found
comfort in knowing that ⓑhis best friend would
live on through his art.
(C) Seeing this, Arias ㉢[challenged / assisted] Picasso
with ⓒhis work, from moving a ladder around
for Picasso to painting some characters. So
Picasso made a joke, “Now I have to sign this
painting Picasso and Arias.” As time passed,
Picasso’s health declined with age. One day,
Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do
with all the paintings and sketches I gave you?”

㉠
㉡
㉢
choices: bargainmovedchallenged
bargainconfusedassisted

solution: ㉠ Arias가 외국 상인에게 자신이 전시한 Picasso의 작품들은 자신과 그의 우정의 상징이기 때문에 단 한 점도 팔지 않겠다 고 말하는 내용이 이어지므로, Picasso의 모든 작품을 팔도록 설득하는 외국 상인에게 흥정을 거절했다는 흐름이 되는 bargain(흥정하다)이 적절하다. ㉡ Arias가 Picasso의 작품들을 전시하기 위해 스페인에 박물 관을 짓겠다고 말했으므로, 이에 Picasso가 감동하여 그를 돕 겠다고 말했다는 흐름이 되는 moved(감동한)가 적절하다. ㉢ Arias는 Picasso를 위해 사다리를 옮기고 작품의 일부 인물 들을 그리는 등의 일을 했으며, Picasso가 이제 그 그림에 Picasso와 Arias라고 서명해야겠다고 농담했다는 내용이 이어 지므로, Arias가 <War and Peace> 작업을 도왔다는 흐름이 되는 assisted(~을 도왔다)가 적절하다.

G: Hello, Alberto. It’s already been quite some time

G: I see! What food do you miss the most?

the lasagna Mom made.
G: Guess what! I know an authentic restaurant run
by an Italian chef. If you have time tonight, let’s
go there together.
B: Sounds great. I’d love to go.
G: Okay, I’ll make a reservation.
B: (A)I really appreciate your kindness. I’m so glad
you’re my friend.
choices: I can't thank you enough.
I’m truly grateful for your help.
I sincerely thank you for your kindness.
I’m really thankful for your thoughtfulness.
I hope you show more kindness to other people.
solution: 한국에서의 삶이 좋지만 이탈리아 가정식 라자냐가 그립다고 말하는 Alberto에게 예진이가 이탈리아 셰프가 운영하는 정통 레스토랑에 함께 가자고 제안하며 예약을 하겠다고 했고, 이에 대해 Alberto가 ‘I really appreciate your kindness.(너의 친절 에 정말 고마워.)’라고 말하며 예진이의 배려에 고마워하는 흐 름이므로, 상대방에게 고마움을 나타내는 것이 아니라 앞으로 더 친절하게 행동하기를 바란다는 의미의 ❺ ‘나는 네가 다른 사람들에게 더 많은 친절함을 보여주기를 바라.’와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

As time passed, Picasso’s health (A)[recovered
declined] with age. One day, Picasso asked Arias,
“What are you going to do with all the paintings
and sketches I gave you?” Arias responded that he
would build a museum in Spain to display the
works. Picasso was moved to hear that and swore
to help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to
see the museum completed, passing away in 1973.
Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in
knowing that his best friend would live on through
his art. A few years later, Arias returned to Spain
and exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit
attracted visitors from all over the world. A foreign
merchant approached Arias one day and attempted
to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works. But
he (B)[refused / consented] to bargain, saying, “Even
if you bring all the money in your country, I will
not sell any of his works to you. His works are
symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me.”
The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The
Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was
finally completed. This was possible because Arias
donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s
works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya.
They comprised a collection of paintings, posters,
ceramics, and other works. Each of them is
(C)[indistinguishable / distinct] from Picasso’s other
works because Picasso carved each one with the
inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend,
Arias). When visitors enter this museum, they
quickly discover that it is more than just a tribute
to honor Picasso’s artistic legacy; it is also a
monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong
friendship.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ feeling → feel (made와 목적어 Picasso에 이어져 ‘make+ 목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, Picasso가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이고, 사역동사 make의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격보어 로 동사원형을 사용하므로, feeling을 동사원형 feel로 고친다.) ⓓ more strongly → stronger (‘~되다’라는 뜻의 2형식 동사 grow의 과 거형 grew에 이어진 보어 자리이며, 보어로 부사(구)는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사의 비교급 more strongly를 형용사의 비교급 stronger로 고친다.) ⓕ preparing → prepared (관계부사 where가 이끄는 절의 동사로 enjoyed가 있으므로, 목적어로 이어진 명사구 Spanish dishes 뒤에 이를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 수 식받는 명사구가 ‘준비된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 행위 주체가 ‘by+명사구’ 형태로 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 preparing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 prepared로 고친다.)

solution: (A) 동사 comprise는 ‘~을 구성[차지]하다’라는 뜻의 타동사로 쓰이거나, 수동 표현인 ’be comprised of ~(~로 이루어지다, ~ 로 구성되다)‘의 형태로 쓰이며, 뒤에 전치사 없이 a collection 이하의 명사구가 목적어로 이어져 있으므로, 타동사의 과거시 제 능동태인 comprised가 적절하다. Can monkeys be friends with horses? How about giraffes and goats? It seems that animals of different species are not compatible with one another, but there is one special friendship that bloomed between a dog and a dolphin. The close friendship between Gunner, a seven-year-old dog, and Delta, a ten-year-old dolphin, is an extraordinary bond that goes beyond the boundaries of their species. Despite their differences in habitat, Gunner and Delta have formed a deep and genuine connection that shows the beauty of friendship between different species. Their first encounter occurred when Gunner’s owner took him to the Dolphin Research Center where Delta lives. As Gunner observed Delta swimming elegantly in the water, he could not help but be fascinated by the dolphin’s grace and friendliness. Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly.

In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, ⓐ[giving / gave] the commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, hoping to help young people find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of them as signposts or approaches ⓑ[that / what] can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you choose to. So here we go.
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome.
(A) Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time.
(B) However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling ⓒ[which / for which] we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
(C) In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it.

gave / that / which
giving / what / which
gave / that / for which

ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can guide your paths in life)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 signposts or approaches를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
ⓒ 타동사 experience의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we experience when ~ the outcome)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a constant feeling을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.

In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, ⓐ[giving / gave] the commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, hoping to help young people find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of them as signposts or approaches ⓑ[that / what] can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you choose to. So here we go.
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome.
(A) Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time.
(B) However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling ⓒ[which / for which] we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
(C) In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 미국 배우이자 제작자인 Matthew McConaughey가 휴스턴 대학교에서 졸업식 연설을 하며 젊은이들이 인생에서 자신의 길을 찾는 데 도움이 되기를 희망했다는 내용 뒤에, 그가 인생에서 배운 몇 가지 중 첫 번째로 행복이 아닌 기쁨을 추구하라고 말하는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 행복은 특정한 결과를 요구한다는 주어진 글의 마지막 문장을 In other words(다시 말해)를 사용해 ‘행복’을 가리키는 it(그것)이 결과에 의존한다고 환언해 부연 설명한 뒤, 행복은 어떤 기준을 달성할 때마다 우리가 즉시 기준을 높이기 때문에 지속시킬 수 없다고 설명한 (C), Therefore(그러므로)를 사용해 행복을 추구할 경우 자주 실망하게 될 것이라는 결과를 제시하는 (A), However(그러나)를 사용해 기쁨은 다르다는 대조적 내용을 연결한 후, 기쁨은 결과에 상관없이 우리가 해야 할 일을 할 때 경험하는 지속적 감정이라고 설명하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

Personally, as an actor, I ⓐused to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance ⓑto be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or ⓒperforming a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, ⓓwhat I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember ⓔthat joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: ‘(예전에는) ~했었다 (지금은 아니다)’라는 뜻의 ‘used to+동사원형’이 쓰여 과거의 상태를 나타낸다.
ⓑ: 목적어가 ‘인정받는’ 대상이므로 ‘need+목적어+to부정사(~가 …할 필요가 있다)’의 to부정사 자리에 수동형 to부정사(to+be+p.p.)가 쓰였다.
ⓒ: 동사 became에 대한 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구를 이끄는 동명사이다.
ⓓ: 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌고 있다.
ⓔ: Remember의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사이다.
solution: ⓒ 전치사 of의 첫 번째 목적어인 동명사구 making a movie와 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 목적어인 동명사구를 이끄는 동명사이며, became은 명사구 ‘the daily act of ~ a role’ 전체를 주어로 하는 동사이다.

오답
① 결과가 먼저, 기쁨은 나중에: 보람 있는 경력의 비결
② 내가 나의 연기 경력과 그 보상에 관심을 끊은 날
④ 한 젊은 배우는 역할을 연기하는 매일의 기술을 어떻게 서서히 터득했는가
⑤ 오늘 열심히 일하라, 그러면 성공이 내일 여러분을 진정으로 행복하게 할 것이다

Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested ⓐto give me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. (A)우리가 어디에 속하는지를 아는 것만큼 우리가 어디에 속하지 않는지를 아는 것도 중요합니다.

You know that some friends ⓓyou hang out really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself ⓔspending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. ⓕKnowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ to give → giving (suggest는 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 동사이므로, suggested 뒤의 목적어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to give를 동명사인 giving으로 고친다.)
ⓓ you hang out → you hang out with (명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어 some friends와 동사구 really don‘t bring out 사이에 쓰여 선행사인 some friends를 수식해야 하므로, 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 who(m) 또는 that이 생략되고 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 한다. 선행사가 ’~와 어울리다‘를 뜻하는 표현인 ‘hang out with ~‘의 전치사 with의 의미상 목적어이므로, 전치사 with를 추가해 you hang out을 you hang out with로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ find와 목적어인 yourself에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, 목적어가 ’보내고 있는‘ 주체이고 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때 현재분사를 사용해 ‘~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다’라는 뜻의 ‘find+목적어+목적격보어(현재분사)’의 형태로 쓰이므로, 현재분사 spending은 알맞다.

solution:
우리의 가장 좋은 면을 끌어내지 않는 친구들은 너무 많이 괴롭히고, 험담을 하거나 의심스러운 행동에 관여할 수도 있다고 말한 뒤, 그들은 우리가 곤경에 처했을 때 우리 곁에 있어 주지 않을 것이라고 했으므로, 글을 제대로 이해하지 못한 사람은 '우리의 가장 좋은 면을 끌어내지 못하는 친구들이더라도 우리가 곤경에 처할 때 우리 곁에 있어 줄 거야.'라고 말한 민준이다.

For each of you, different courses and topics ⓐyou study them will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know ⓑthat they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education (A)[rises / diminishes] unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and ⓒsupporting your families. But it also means something much (B)[more / less] significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world ⓓwhere you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever ⓔwent hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or ⓕhelping others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I (C)[give to / get from] others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ you study them → you study (앞의 명사구 different courses and topics가 타동사 study(~을 공부하다)의 의미상 목적어이므로, 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that이 생략되고, study 뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태로 선행사인 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 study 뒤의 them을 삭제하여 you study them을 you study로 고친다.)
ⓓ where → which[that] 또는 where 삭제 (전치사 in의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you live in)을 이끌어, 선행사인 the community and world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 where를 목적격 관계대명사 which나 that으로 고치거나, 목적격 관계대명사는 생략 가능하므로 where를 삭제한다.)
*원래 지문에는 생략되어 있음
ⓕ helping → help (조동사 would 뒤의 동사원형 give와 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, helping을 동사원형 help로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사(구)가 올 자리이며, go는 ‘~하게 되다’를 뜻하는 2형식 동사로 쓰여 형용사를 보어로 취할 수 있으므로, 흐름상 과거시제로 쓰인 went 뒤에 형용사 hungry가 보어로 쓰인 went hungry는 알맞다.

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an ⓐasset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of ⓑrejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to ⓒadmit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, ⓓgrabbing your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will ⓔlose the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by ⓕeliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.

If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. (A) This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. (B) In fact, setting high standards is one of the most common habits shared by successful people. (C) Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. (D) However, joy is a different thing. (E) It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor (F)______, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 행복은 결과에 의존하는 감정적 반응이며, 기준을 달성할 때마다 즉시 기준을 높여 행복을 지속시킬 수 없기 때문에 행복을 추구할 경우 자주 실망하게 되는 반면, 기쁨은 결과와 관계없이 우리가 해야 할 일을 할 때 경험하는 지속적인 감정이라는 내용이므로, 높은 기준과 성공의 관계를 언급하는 (B) ‘사실, 높은 기준을 세우는 것은 성공한 사람들에 의해 공유되는 가장 흔한 습관 중 하나이다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 무관하다.

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Choosing the right friends is the key to leading a healthier life.
We should accept every opportunity that brings us greater rewards.
We need to figure out our real identity before deciding what to give up.
Knowing our strengths matters more than knowing the areas where we fall short.
Discovering our true selves usually begins by removing what does not truly represent us.
solution:

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because ______. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: it keeps us safe by warning us about real physical danger
it reminds us that some goals are simply out of our reach
it allows us to predict how others will react to our requests
it tends to disappear on its own once we stop paying attention to it
it makes us feel a greater need to challenge ourselves to get over it
solution:
두려움을 부정하는 것은 그것을 극복할 기회를 버리는 것이며, 두려움에 맞서고 그것을 인정하면 극복할 용기를 찾게 될 것이라고 했으므로, 두려움은 그것을 극복하도록 스스로에게 도전할 필요성을 키워 주기 때문에 자산이라고 생각한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ⑤ '그것은 우리가 그것을 극복하도록 우리 스스로에게 도전할 더 큰 필요성을 느끼게 한다'가 알맞다.

④ 그것은 우리가 그것에 주의를 기울이는 것을 멈추면 저절로 사라지는 경향이 있다

A: Ms. Lee, I have already read your article. What is an AI domestic assistant exactly?
B: It’s an AI-powered device ⓐ[designing / designed] to help with household tasks.
A: (A)I’m pretty sure that it will help people with laundry, washing dishes, and organizing their closets.
B: Yes, exactly. I can’t wait for this AI machine ⓑ[to come / coming] out. It is expected ⓒ[to be / being] released on June 1.

위 대화의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: designed coming being
designing coming to be
designed to come being
designing to come to be
designed to come to be
solution:
ⓐ 수식을 받는 앞의 명사구 an AI-powered device가 타동사 design(~을 고안하다)의 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘be designed+to부정사(~하도록 고안되다)’의 수동 표현을 이루는 to부정사구가 이어져 있으므로 과거분사 designed가 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사구 can’t wait와 to부정사의 의미상주어인 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for this AI machine에 이어져 있으므로 ’~가 …하기를 기다릴 수 없을 지경이다, ~가 …하기를 몹시 기다리다’라는 뜻의 ’can’t wait+for+목적격+to부정사‘를 이루는 to부정사 to come이 알맞다.
ⓒ 동사 expect는 ’expect+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …할 것으로 예상하다)‘의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하며 수동 표현은 ’be expected+to부정사(…할 것으로 예상되다)‘로 나타내므로, 수동태 is expected 뒤에 to부정사구를 이루는 to be가 알맞다. 참고로, 주어 It이 가리키는 this AI machine이 ’출시되는‘ 대상이므로 수동형 to부정사(to+be+p.p.)가 쓰인다.

This movie, set in 2001, ⓐrealistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that (A)______. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to ⓑunderstand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw ⓒlogical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, has become a ⓓdream. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a ⓔcompetent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

(A) It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and assigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.

(B) AI robots are also used in operating rooms. Based on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct cognitive activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: AI 기반 프로그램이나 로봇이 의료 산업에서 널리 사용되고 있으며 일부 AI 프로그램은 암에 걸릴 가능성을 예측할 수 있을 정도로 개선되어 왔다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, also(또한)를 사용해 AI 로봇은 수술실에서도 사용되며 수집된 데이터를 기반으로 음성 인식, 의사 결정, 문제 해결 등과 같은 인지 활동을 수행할 수 있다고 설명한 (B), 앞서 언급한 AI 수술 로봇을 they(그들)로 가리켜 그들이 절개나 봉합과 같은 기본적인 처치를 수행할 수 있다는 점을 추가 설명한 뒤, 또 다른 예로 환자의 상태가 악화될 가능성을 예측하는 AI 시스템의 개발을 제시하는 (C), 앞서 언급된 AI 시스템을 It(그것)으로 가리켜 그것이 환자의 프로필과 데이터를 분석하여 중환자실로의 이송 필요성을 나타내는 점수를 부여한다고 구체적으로 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also enables them to make what they intended to express ⓐ[come / to come] alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through ⓑ[which / that] actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when ⓒ[providing / provided] with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program (A)[accelerates / prolongs] the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to (B)[learn / teach] how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly (C)[realistic / unrealistic]. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, it is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: to come which provided
come which providing
to come that providing
come which provided
to come that provided
solution:
ⓐ 사역동사 make와 목적어인 명사절 what they intended to express에 이어져 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이므로, 동사원형 come이 알맞다.
ⓑ 전치사 through의 목적어 자리에 쓰였으며, 뒤에 완전한 절(actors‘ ~ younger)이 이어지므로, ’전치사+관계대명사+완전한 절‘ 형태로 앞 절의 an AI-based program을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루는 목적격 관계대명사가 올 자리이며, 전치사 뒤에 관계대명사 that은 쓰이지 않으므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.
ⓒ 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태인 ’접속사+분사~‘ 구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 생략된 주어 it(=the AI program)이 ’제공받는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 ’provide ~ with …(~에게 …을 제공하다)‘의 목적어 없이 전치사 with가 바로 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ’~ be provided with …(~가 …을 제공받다)‘의 과거분사 provided가 알맞다.

While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program (A)[accelerates / prolongs] the process. It was then trained to (B)[learn / teach] how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: accelerates teach unrealistic
prolongs learn realistic
accelerates learn unrealistic
prolongs teach realistic
accelerates learn realistic
solution:
(A) 다양한 연령대의 다양한 얼굴 이미지를 생성하는 기존의 기술들은 방대한 과정을 요구했다고 한 뒤에 However(그러나)로 이어지므로, 새로 개발된 자동화 프로그램은 그 과정을 빠르게 한다는 대조적인 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 accelerates(~을 가속화한다)가 알맞다.
prolongs ~을 연장한다
(B) 프로그램에 18세부터 85세까지 이르는 얼굴 사진 수천 장이 입력으로 축적되었고, 이후 그것이 노화의 원리를 도출했다고 했으므로, 수천 장의 얼굴 사진을 통해 나이에 따른 얼굴의 변화 양상을 프로그램이 학습하도록 훈련되었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 learn(~을 배우다)이 알맞다.
teach ~을 가르치다
(C) 그 결과물이 배우들이 다양한 얼굴 표정을 지어도 유지되고, 그것의 편리함과 자연스러움 때문에 영화 제작에 널리 활용될 것으로 기대된다는 내용이 이어지므로, AI 기반 프로그램이 매우 사실적인 출력물을 만들어 낼 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 realistic(사실적인)이 알맞다.

B: Cathy, what are you looking at?
G: I’m looking at the painting, Space Opera Theatre.
B: Can I see?
G: Sure. Here you go. It won first place in an art competition.
B: Wow, it looks so aesthetically ⓐ[pleasing / pleased]! Who is the painter with such talent?
G: Actually, it was painted by using an AI art generator.
B: What is an AI art generator exactly?
G: It’s an artificial intelligence program ⓑ[that / what] produces digital images.
B: Unbelievable! How can it do that?
G: When a person provides a written text, the AI software converts it into images. Then they are printed on canvas.
B: This is so fascinating! I’ve never imagined AI ⓒ[using / being used] in the field of art!

pleased / that / being used
pleasing / that / using

pleasing / that / being used
solution:
ⓐ 2형식 동사로 쓰인 looks의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 올 자리이며, the painting, Space Opera Theatre를 가리키는 주어 it이 ‘즐거움을 주는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 형태의 형용사 pleasing이 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 수식받는 앞의 명사구와 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 described로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, set in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that (A)human imagination goes far beyond reality. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. (B)그 당시에 영화에서만 보였던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 현실이 되었습니다. In 2008, the International Space Station, a large spacecraft orbiting Earth, started to use an AI robot named CIMON. It is a floating spherical robot that can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)human imagination goes far beyond reality가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Human technology always develops faster than scientific imagination.
Artificial intelligence was already fully operational in space long before 1968.
Space exploration relies heavily on historical events rather than futuristic visions.
Realistic movies prevent scientists from introducing innovative ideas into space programs.
Creative ideas and fiction can anticipate real-world developments long before they occur.
solution:
다른 행성으로 향하는 우주선 속 과학자들의 집단을 사실적으로 묘사한 영화 <2001: A Space Odyssey>는 최초의 달 착륙보다 1년 앞선 1968년에 개봉되었으며, 당시 영화에서만 볼 수 있었던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 이후 국제우주정거장의 AI 로봇 CIMON으로 현실이 되었다고 했으므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘인간의 상상력이 현실을 훨씬 넘어선다’는 인간의 창의적 아이디어와 상상력이 미래의 세계를 예견할 수 있음을 뜻한다고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 (A)가 의미하는 바로 ⑤ ‘창의적인 아이디어와 허구는 현실 세계의 발전이 일어나기 훨씬 전에 그것을 예견할 수 있다.’가 알맞다.
오답
① 인간의 기술은 항상 과학적 상상력보다 더 빠르게 발전한다.
② 인공지능은 1968년 훨씬 이전에 이미 우주에서 완전히 작동하고 있었다.
③ 우주 탐사는 미래지향적 비전보다 역사적 사건에 크게 의존한다.
④ 사실적인 영화는 과학자들이 우주 프로그램에 혁신적인 아이디어를 도입하는 것을 방지한다.

body:
Minority Report
Minority Report, ⓐa film setting in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes.
(A) However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, ⓑdevices employ AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.
(B) For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems ⓒprovide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices ⓓhave already been developed.
(C) There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After ⓔscanning him and identifying who is he, the advertising system offers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we frequently encounter ⓕpersonalized advertisements provided by AI.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ setting → set (주어 Minority Report와 동사구 was released 사이에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 주어와 동격을 이루는 명사구가 ‘명사구+분사구’ 형태로 올 수 있으나, 명사구 a film이 ‘설정된’ 대상이므로 수동 표현인 ‘be set in ~ ((특정 장소·시대 등)을 배경으로 하다)’의 과거분사 set 뒤에 전치사구(in ~ 2050)가 이어져 분사구를 이루도록 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 setting을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 set으로 고친다.)
ⓑ employ → employing 또는 which[that] employ (주어 devices 뒤에 접속사 없이 두 개의 동사구가 연달아 쓰일 수 없으므로, 주어 devices와 동사구 have overcome 사이에 주어를 수식하는 분사구나 관계사절이 온 구조가 되어야 한다. 수식받는 devices가 ‘활용하는’ 주체이므로 employ를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 employing으로 고치거나, 적절한 주격 관계대명사 which[that]를 추가하고 선행사가 되는 복수명사 devices에 수일치한 복수동사 employ를 사용해 which[that] employ로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 employing이 쓰였음
ⓔ is he → he is (전치사 After의 목적어로 동명사 scanning과 identifying이 이끄는 두 개의 동명사구가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 것은 알맞으나, identifying의 목적어 자리에 의문사 who가 이끄는 명사절이 의문사 뒤 평서문의 간접의문문 어순으로 와야 하므로, ‘be동사+주어’가 아닌 ‘주어+be동사’의 순서가 되도록 is he를 he is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓕ 타동사 encounter의 목적어로 명사구 personalized advertisements가 쓰인 것과, 앞의 명사구가 AI에 의해 ‘제공되는’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 provided 뒤에 ’by+명사‘ 형태의 by AI가 이어져 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 과거분사구를 이룬 것은 모두 알맞다.

solution: 영화 <Minority Report>에 사람의 눈을 스캔해 개인을 식별하는 AI 기반 광고가 등장한다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 주인공이 쇼핑몰에 들어가는 장면을 구체적으로 묘사한 뒤 오늘날 우리가 AI가 제공하는 개인 맞춤형 광고를 자주 접한다고 하는 (C), For instance(예를 들어)를 사용해 온라인 쇼핑몰, 영상 공유 플랫폼, 소셜 미디어의 AI 시스템이 이전 검색이나 온라인 활동을 바탕으로 광고를 제공하는 예를 들고 눈을 스캔해 사람을 식별하는 장치가 이미 개발되었다고 설명하는 (B), However(그러나) 뒤에 앞서 언급한 devices를 those로 가리켜 AI 기술을 사용하지 않는 장치들의 치명적인 한계를 제시한 뒤 AI를 사용하는 장치들은 그 한계를 극복했다고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
These days, AI-based programs or robots are widely used in the medical industry. Some AI programs have been refined to the point that they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also predict the chance of getting cancer. AI robots are also used in operating rooms. Based on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct cognitive activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct elementary operations such as cutting and stitching patients undergoing surgery. Another example is the development of an AI system to ______. It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and assigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: reduce the overall cost of surgical procedures in hospitals
replace human doctors completely in intensive care units
anticipate when a hospitalized patient’s health may decline
schedule routine checkups for patients who have been discharged
automatically prescribe medication without a doctor’s approval
solution:
AI 시스템이 환자의 프로필과 데이터를 분석하여 집중 치료실로의 이송 필요성을 나타내는 점수를 부여하고, 점수가 일정 수준에 도달하면 의료진이 개입한다고 했으므로, 입원 환자의 상태가 악화될 시점을 예측하는 AI 시스템을 소개하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘입원 환자의 건강이 언제 악화될 수 있는지를 예상하다’가 알맞다.
본문변형
forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse → anticipate a potential decline in a hospitalized patient’s health
오답
① 병원에서 수술 절차의 전반적인 비용을 줄이다
② 중환자실에서 인간 의사를 완전히 대체하다
④ 퇴원한 환자에 대한 정기 검진 일정을 잡다
⑤ 의사의 승인 없이 약을 자동으로 처방하다

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also ⓐ[enables / enabling] them to make what they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through which actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained ⓑ[to learn / learning] how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to (A)______, it is expected ⓒ[that / what] this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: enables / to learn / what
enabling / to learn / what
enables / to learn / that
enabling / learning / that
enables / learning / that
solution:
ⓐ 상관접속사 ‘not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)’에 의해 주어 it에 대한 현재형 단수동사 assists와 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 현재형 단수동사 enables가 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사 train은 ‘train+목적어+to부정사(~을 …하도록 훈련하다)’의 형태로 쓰이며 수동 표현은 ‘~ be trained+to부정사(~가 …하도록 훈련받다)’로 나타내므로, 수동태가 쓰인 동사구 was then trained 뒤에 to부정사인 to learn이 알맞다.
ⓒ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리에서 완전한 절(this ~ filmmaking)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ which → where 또는 in which (관계대명사 which가 완전한 절(a boy ~ robot)을 이끌 수 없으므로, 관계사절이 수식하는 선행사 a scene에 어울리는 관계부사 where 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 in which로 고친다. 그 외, Baymax와 동격 관계를 이루는 명사구 a personal medical aid AI robot이 동격의 콤마(,)로 연결된 것은 알맞다.)
*원래 지문에는 where가 쓰였음
ⓑ That → What (완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 That 뒤에 타동사 discovers의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(it discovers within seconds)이 이어질 수 없으며, 흐름상 보어인 a wound in his arm을 강조하는 ‘What+주어+동사~+be동사 … (~한 것은 바로 …이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문을 이루어야 하므로, That을 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끌 수 있는 관계대명사 What으로 고친다. 그 외, 앞 문장의 단수명사구 The robot을 가리키는 단수 지시대명사 it이 관계사절의 주어로 쓰인 것과, 관계대명사 what이 의미상 목적어 역할을 하므로 단수동사로 수일치한 능동태 discovers가 뒤에 목적어 없이 쓰인 것은 모두 알맞다.)
ⓔ undergone → undergoing (such as(~와 같은)의 목적어 자리에 두 개의 동명사 cutting과 stitching이 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되고 뒤에 공통의 목적어 patients가 이어진 것은 알맞으며, 명사 patients를 수식하는 분사구가 뒤에 이어질 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사 patients가 타동사 undergo(~을 받다)의 주체이고 명사 surgery가 목적어에 해당하므로, 과거분사 undergone을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 undergoing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 선행사에 point가 있을 때 관계부사 where 대신 관계부사 대용의 that이 흔히 쓰이므로, 관계부사 대용의 that이 완전한 절(they ~ accurately)을 이끌어 선행사 the point를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 것은 알맞다. 복수명사구 Some AI programs를 가리키는 복수 대명사 they가 관계사절의 주어로 쓰이고, 조동사 can 뒤에 ’not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)‘ 형태의 상관접속사를 이루는 not only와 동사원형 identify가 쓰인 것과, 목적어 cancer 뒤에 동사를 수식하는 두 개의 부사 quickly와 accurately가 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있는 것 또한 모두 알맞다.

Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After scanning him and identifying who he is, the advertising system offers products that may be appealing to him. Nowadays, we (A)[frequently / hardly] encounter personalized advertisements provided by AI. For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems provide us with advertisements (B)[based on / regardless of] our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, devices employing AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous (C)[development / criticism] of this technology up until now.

choices: frequently / based on / development
hardly / based on / development
frequently / based on / criticism
hardly / regardless of / development
frequently / regardless of / criticism
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 For instance(예를 들어)를 사용해 많은 온라인 쇼핑몰, 동영상 공유 플랫폼, 소셜 미디어가 AI를 사용한다는 예를 들고 있으므로, 오늘날 우리가 AI가 제공하는 개인 맞춤형 광고를 흔히 접한다는 흐름이 되는 frequently(자주, 빈번히)가 알맞다.

body:
In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, gave the commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, hoping to help young people ⓐto find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of ㉠them as signposts or approaches that can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you choose to. So here we go.
Number One. ⓑSeek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, ㉡it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. (A) This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. (B) Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. (C) It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. (D) Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome. (E)
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, ⓒthought, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance ⓓto acknowledge.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role ⓔto become its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever ⓕhave before. However, what I realized was ⓖthat aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making ㉢it.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 4개이다.
ⓒ thought → thinking (앞의 완전한 절(I used to have ~ the outcome)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 I가 ‘생각한’ 주체이므로, thought를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 thinking으로 고친다.)
ⓓ to acknowledge → to be acknowledged (‘need+목적어+to부정사(~가 …할 필요가 있다)’를 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 목적어 my performance가 ‘인정받는’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, to acknowledge를 수동형 to부정사(to+be+p.p.)인 to be acknowledged로 고친다.)
ⓔ to become → became (구접속사 As soon as(~하자마자)가 이끄는 부사절의 주어 the daily act of making a movie or performing a role에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 흐름상 과거의 일이므로, to become을 과거동사 became으로 고친다.)
ⓕ have → had (유사관계대명사의 역할을 하는 than(~보다)이 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 주절 동사(received)가 나타내는 과거시점 이전(before)의 경험을 나타내야 하므로, 과거완료(had+p.p.)인 had received에서 반복되는 과거분사 received가 생략된 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 have를 had로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 준사역동사는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취해 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)’의 형태로 쓰이므로, help와 목적어 young people 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to find는 알맞다.
본문변형 find →to find

Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was ⓐthrilling and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither ⓑWooderson should. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. ⓒDefine ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places ⓓwhat are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are (A)______, you will only have important things that ⓔleave in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지 못한 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: ⓐ: thrilling → thrilled
ⓑ: Wooderson should → should Wooderson
ⓒ: Define → Defining
ⓓ: what → where
ⓔ: leave → left
solution:
ⓓ what → that[which] (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(are healthier for you)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 more places를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이나 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
ⓔ leave → are left (주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, 흐름상 현재시제로 선행사인 복수명사구 important things에 수일치한 복수동사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수와 태를 일치시켜야 하며, 선행사가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로 현재시제 수동태를 써야 한다. 따라서 leave를 are left로 고친다.)
본문변형 left → that are left
오답
ⓐ 주어 I가 ‘흥분시키는’ 주체가 아니라 ‘흥분된’ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 형태의 형용사 thrilling을 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 thrilled로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓑ 부정어 neither가 문장이나 절의 맨 앞에 쓰일 때 도치가 적용되어 조동사가 있는 경우 ‘neither+조동사+주어’의 어순으로 쓰이므로, Wooderson should를 should Wooderson으로 고친 것은 알맞다. 참고로, 주어 뒤에 have been there가 반복을 피하기 위해 생략되었다.
ⓒ 동사 helps에 대한 주어 자리에 동명사(구)나 to부정사(구)가 와야 하므로, 동사원형 Define을 동명사 Defining으로 고친 것은 알맞다.

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to (A)[scare / comfort] myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here ⓐto speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ⓑus to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed ⓒadmit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t (B)[accept / deny] that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, (C)[confront / ignore] your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage ⓓto overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing ⓔthat you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, ⓕovercoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: scare accept confront
scare accept ignore
scare deny confront
comfort deny ignore
comfort deny confront
solution:
(A) 앞서 두려움을 인정하라고 했으며, 자신은 매일 아침 출근 전에 긴장하고, 오늘 연설 전에도 긴장했다고 설명하므로, 하루에 적어도 한 번은 스스로를 겁주어 두려움을 마주한다는 흐름이 되는 scare(~을 놀라게 하다, ~을 무섭게 하다)가 알맞다.
comfort ~을 안심시키다, ~을 위로하다
(B) 두려움을 인정하라고 조언하는 흐름이므로, 그것이 별것 아닌 것처럼 굴지 말고 그것의 존재를 부정하지 말라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 don’t 뒤에 deny(~을 부정하다)가 알맞다.
accept ~을 받아들이다
(C) 뒤에 그것을 극복할 용기를 발견하게 된다는 결과를 제시하므로, 두려움에 맞서라는 흐름이 되는 confront(~에 맞서다)가 알맞다.
ignore ~을 무시하다

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. (A)[Which / Whichever] way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking (B)[what / that] you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means ⓐ______. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors (C)[that / which] needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: Which what which
Whichever that that
Whichever that which
Which that which
Whichever what that
solution:
(A) 주절(I know ~ journey) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 부사절이 와야 하며, 뒤에 수식받는 명사 way가 이어져 있으므로, ‘~하는 어느 …든지 상관없이’를 뜻하는 ‘whichever+명사+주어+동사~’ 형태의 양보 부사절을 이끌 수 있는 복합관계형용사 Whichever가 알맞다.
(B) 타동사로 쓰인 know의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you already know)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 the places and ways of thinking을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
본문변형 (B)는 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 원래 지문에서는 생략되어 있었음
(C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(needed them)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사 neighbors를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 사람 선행사와 쓰일 수 있는 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. (A)[Which / Whichever] way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking (B)[what / that] you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means ⓐ______. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors (C)[that / which] needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: putting your education toward earning more degrees for yourself
beating others in competition by relying on your education
helping to improve your local area and the wider world
earning enough money to support yourself and your family
gaining fame and public recognition through your knowledge
solution:
앞서 바람직한 활용은 생계를 꾸리고 가족을 부양하는 것을 포함하지만 그것은 또한 훨씬 더 중요한 것을 의미한다고 했으며, 뒤에서 그러한 개선이 대법관이 되는 것처럼 크거나 공적인 방식일 필요는 없다고 하며, 주변의 누구도 굶주리지 않게 함으로써 지역사회를 더 나은 곳으로 만든 할머니와 이웃을 도운 어머니의 예를 들고 있으므로, 바람직한 활용은 자신이 사는 지역사회와 세상을 더 나아지게 하는 데 기여하는 것을 의미한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ '여러분의 지역과 더 넓은 세상을 개선하는 데 도움을 주는 것'이 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 지문에서 ‘contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in’이었음

② 여러분의 교육에 의지해 경쟁에서 다른 사람들을 이기는 것

body:
Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. (A)[Which / Whichever] way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking (B)[what / that] you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means ⓐ______. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors (C)[that / which] needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
• No Latin-American had served as a US Supreme Court justice before Sotomayor.
• Studying various subjects will help people find their way through life differently.
• Earning a living is excluded from what counts as good use of education.
• Making sure no one nearby went without food, Sotomayor's grandmother improved the lives of those in her community.
• Sotomayor's mother, a doctor by profession, provided medical care to her neighbors.
• Sotomayor considers her family's lesson less important than what she learned at school.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은 총 3개이다.
교육의 바람직한 활용은 생계를 꾸리고 가족을 부양하는 것을 포함한다고 했으므로, ‘생계를 꾸리는 것은 교육의 바람직한 활용에 해당하는 것에서 제외된다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
자신의 어머니는 간호조무사로서 주사가 필요한 이웃들에게 주사를 놓거나 혈압을 재거나 붕대를 교체하는 일로 사람들을 도왔다고 했으므로, ‘직업이 의사였던 Sotomayor의 어머니는 이웃들에게 의료 서비스를 제공했다.’ 또한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
Sotomayor의 가족은 그녀가 직업으로서 무슨 일을 하는가가 아니라 다른 사람에게 무엇을 베푸는가로 행복을 측정하라고 가르쳤으며, 그것은 자신이 인생에서 발견한 가장 중요한 교훈이자 가장 깊은 의미의 원천이라고 했으므로, ‘Sotomayor는 가족의 교훈을 학교에서 배운 것보다 덜 중요하게 여긴다.’도 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
제시문
• 라틴계 미국인 중 누구도 Sotomayor 이전에 미국 대법관을 지낸 적이 없었다.
• 다양한 과목을 공부하는 것은 사람들이 삶에서 각기 다르게 자신의 길을 찾도록 도울 것이다.
• 생계를 꾸리는 것은 교육의 바람직한 활용에 해당하는 것에서 제외(→포함)된다.
• 주변의 누구도 먹을 것 없이 지내지 않도록 확실히 함으로써, Sotomayor의 할머니는 지역사회 사람들의 삶을 개선했다.
• 직업이 의사(→간호조무사)였던 Sotomayor의 어머니는 이웃들에게 의료 서비스를 제공했다.
• Sotomayor는 가족의 교훈을 학교에서 배운 것보다 덜 중요하게(→인생에서 발견한 가장 중요한 교훈이자 가장 깊은 의미의 원천으로) 여긴다.

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.

Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
Focusing on the work itself, not the results, lets us find the ______ always present in the ______.
solution: [제시문] 결과가 아닌 일 자체에 초점을 맞추는 것은 우리가 과정 중에 항상 있는 기쁨을 발견할 수 있게 한다.

Minority Report
Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. (C) Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. (D) They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now. (E)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘반면에, AI를 이용하는 기기들은 이러한 한계를 극복했습니다.’라는 뜻으로, On the other hand(반면에)를 사용해 앞서 언급한 한계와 대조되는 내용을 제시하는 흐름이므로, this limitation(이러한 한계)이 가리키는 내용, 즉 AI 기술을 사용하지 않는 기기들은 사람이 가만히 서 있을 때만 그 사람을 식별할 수 있다는 한계를 설명한 내용의 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 devices employing AI를 They로 가리켜 그것들이 걷고 있는 사람들의 눈도 스캔할 수 있다고 설명하는 내용 앞인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, ⓐsetting in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that human imagination goes far beyond reality. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, ⓑcalled “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance ⓒto understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts ⓓconducting experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, ⓔhas become a reality. (A)2008년, 지구의 궤도를 도는 대형 우주선인 국제우주정거장에서 CIMON이라는 이름의 AI 로봇을 사용하기 시작했습니다. It is a floating spherical robot ⓕthat can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, ⓖweighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when ⓗasked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ setting → set (주어 This movie에 대한 동사로 describes가 있으므로 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 의미상 주어인 This movie가 ‘설정된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘be set in ~ ((특정 장소·시대 등)을 배경으로 하다)’의 전치사구 in 2001이 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 setting을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 set으로 고친다.)
ⓓ conducting → conduct 또는 to conduct (help가 준사역동사로 쓰여 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)’의 5형식 구문을 이룰 때 목적격보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)이나 to부정사가 쓰이므로, help와 목적어 the astronauts 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 conducting을 동사원형 conduct나 to부정사인 to conduct로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 conduct가 쓰였음
오답
ⓑ 완전한 절(the ship has a computer system)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 흐름상 앞 절의 명사구 a computer system을 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 a computer system이 ‘불리는’ 대상이고 뒤에 ‘call+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …라고 부르다)’의 목적격보어에 해당하는 “HAL-9000”가 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be called+보어(…라고 불리다)’의 과거분사 called는 알맞다.
ⓗ 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태인 ‘접속사+분사‘ 구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리로, 생략된 주어 it(=the robot)이 ’요청받는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 asked는 알맞다.

③ 그 영화는 우주선을 제어하는 컴퓨터 시스템을 등장시킨다.

body:
Big Hero 6
This is a science fiction animation that was released in 2014. There is a scene in the movie where a boy meets Baymax, a personal medical aid AI robot. The robot scans the boy’s body to detect potential health problems ⓐ[using / used] its sensors and cameras. ⓑ[That / What] it discovers within seconds is a wound in his arm. It administers medicine on the wound. In ⓒ[another / other] scene where he has a mood swing, Baymax checks his hormone levels to determine the cause of his mood swing.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: using What another
using What other
using That another
used What other
used That another
solution:
ⓐ 앞의 완전한 절(The robot ~ problems)에 연결되어 동시동작(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 주절 주어(The robot)와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 its sensors and cameras가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 using이 알맞다.
ⓑ 문장의 주어 자리에서 타동사 discovers의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(it discovers within seconds)을 이끌고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끌며, 흐름상 보어인 a wound in his arm을 강조하는 ‘What+주어+동사~+be동사 … (~한 것은 바로 …이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문을 이루는 관계대명사 What이 알맞다.
ⓒ 뒤에 가산명사의 단수형인 scene이 이어져 있으므로, ‘또 하나의 ~’라는 의미로 단수명사(구)를 수식할 수 있는 another가 알맞다. 참고로, other는 ‘다른 ~’이라는 의미로 복수명사(구)나 불가산명사를 수식한다.

In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. These results are (E)maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, ⓔit is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

solution:
(B) simple(간단한) → complicated(복잡한), extensive(방대한) 등

body:
The film production industry extensively (A)utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also ⓐenables them to make that they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, ⓑthrough which actors’ faces on the screen is aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. ⓒWhile there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required a (B)simple process. However, ⓓthe newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to learn how faces change as people age, and (C)derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can (D)manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are (E)maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, ⓔit is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ that → what (상관접속사 ‘not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)’에 의해 단수동사 assists와 병렬연결을 이루는 단수동사 enables가 쓰이고 뒤에 복수명사 producers를 가리키는 복수대명사 them과 to부정사 to make가 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 수 있게 하다)’의 5형식 구조를 이룬 것과, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리에 ‘come alive(생생하게 살아나다)’의 동사원형 come이 쓰인 것은 모두 알맞으나, 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that 뒤에 타동사 express의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they intended to express)이 올 수 없으므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’을 나타내는 관계대명사 what이 뒤의 불완전한 절을 이끌어 동사 make의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루도록 that을 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
ⓑ is → are (콤마(,) 뒤에 전치사 through와 목적격 관계대명사 which가 쓰이고 완전한 절(actors‘ ~ younger)이 이어져 앞 절의 an AI-based program을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이룬 것과, 관계사절의 주어 ’actors‘ ~ screen‘이 ’늙어 보이거나 더 젊어 보이게 만들어진‘ 대상이므로 수동태(be동사+p.p.)가 쓰여 be동사 뒤에 두 개의 과거분사가 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬로 연결되고 과거분사 made 뒤에 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be made+보어(형용사)(~가 …하게 만들어지다)’를 이루는 비교급 형태의 형용사 younger가 이어진 것은 모두 알맞으나, 관계사절의 핵심주어인 actors‘ faces가 복수명사구이므로 수일치를 위해 단수형 be동사 is를 복수형인 are로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ ’~라는 것이 예상된다‘라는 뜻으로 ’it is expected that+완전한 절‘ 형태의 ’가주어(it)-진주어(that절)‘ 구문이 쓰인 것과, 진주어절의 주어 this technique이 ’반영되는‘ 대상이므로 조동사 will과 함께 ’incorporate ~ in …(~을 …에 반영[추가]하다)‘의 수동 표현인 ’~ be incorporated in …(~가 …에 반영[추가]되다)‘이 쓰이고 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 부사 widely가 쓰여 뒤의 과거분사를 수식하는 것은 모두 알맞다.

body:
Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After scanning him and identifying who he is, the advertising system ______. Nowadays, we frequently encounter personalized advertisements provided by AI. For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems provide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, devices employing AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: asks him to stand still for accurate scanning
offers products that may be appealing to him
deletes his previous online search history for his privacy
blocks unwanted advertisements from appearing on the screen
tracks his physical movements to prevent his entry to the mall
solution:

① 정확한 스캔을 위해 그에게 가만히 서 있으라고 요청합니다
③ 그의 사생활을 위해 그의 이전 온라인 검색 기록을 삭제합니다

body:
Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies described in films are now a (A)[reality / fantasy]. One of them is self-driving cars. In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. The taxi is (B)[capable / incapable] of driving itself without any human intervention. Having seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars. Luckily, self-driving cars are being developed and certain versions are already on the road. Additionally, many other AI technologies from movies are either (C)[in use / out of use] or under development.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: reality capable in use
fantasy capable in use
reality capable out of use
fantasy incapable in use
reality incapable out of use
solution:
(A) 글 뒷부분에서 자율주행 자동차가 개발되고 있는 중이며 특정 모델은 이미 도로에서 운행되고 있다고 했으므로, 영화 속에서 묘사된 여러 인공지능(AI) 기술은 이제 현실이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 reality(현실)가 알맞다.
fantasy 환상, 공상
(B) 영화 <Total Recall>에서 택시 기사는 그 차량의 컴퓨터 시스템이며 인간의 개입이 없다는 내용이 언급되므로, 스스로 운전할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 capable(~할 수 있는)이 알맞다.
incapable ~할 수 없는
(C) 자율주행 자동차가 개발되고 있으며, 특정 모델은 이미 도로에서 운행되고 있다고 한 뒤에 Additionally(게다가)로 이어지므로, 영화 속의 많은 다른 AI 기술이 사용되거나 개발되고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 in use(사용되고 있는)가 알맞다.
out of use 사용되지 않는

body:
AI in movies and our future
AI has been progressing rapidly over the years, and its potential is only beginning to be fully recognized. It is certain that AI will continue to play a significant role in more and more aspects of our lives. (A)______, these days, a lot of movies feature various kinds of AI. Some AI robots have personalities and emotionally engage with people in the same way that humans do. (B)______, some AI characters are physically indistinguishable from humans. ⓐ이런 영화들은 보기에 재밌을 뿐만 아니라 영감을 주기도 합니다. They show us what AI might be like in the future and how it could affect us. What AI technology from a movie do you think will be used in our lives in the future?

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: However Nonetheless
Otherwise For example
Accordingly Furthermore
Nevertheless Additionally
Consequently Still
solution:
(A) AI가 계속해서 우리 삶의 점점 더 많은 측면에서 중요한 역할을 할 것이라는 것이 확실하다는 이유를 앞에서 제시한 뒤, 요즘 많은 영화들이 다양한 종류의 AI를 특징으로 삼는다는 결과를 연결하므로, 인과관계를 나타내는 Accordingly(그에 따라, 그 결과로) 또는 Consequently(그 결과, 따라서)가 알맞다.
(B) 일부 AI 로봇이 성격을 가지고 있고 인간이 하는 방식으로 사람들과 감정적으로 소통한다고 한 뒤에 일부 AI 캐릭터는 신체적으로 인간과 구분이 안 된다는 추가적인 설명을 덧붙이므로, ’더욱이, 게다가‘라는 뜻의 Furthermore 또는 Additionally가 알맞다.

① 하지만 그럼에도 불구하고
② 그렇지 않으면 예를 들어
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 더욱이, 게다가
⑤ 그 결과, 따라서 그래도

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, set in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that human imagination goes far beyond reality.

(A) Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, has become a reality. In 2008, the International Space Station, a large spacecraft orbiting Earth, started to use an AI robot named CIMON.

(B) It is a floating spherical robot that can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

(C) In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 영화 <2001: A Space Odyssey>는 최초의 달 착륙보다 1년 먼저 개봉되었으며 이는 인간의 상상력이 현실을 훨씬 넘어섬을 의미한다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 이 영화에 등장하는 HAL-9000이라는 컴퓨터 시스템의 역할과 기능을 설명하고 그것이 우주선의 결함이 있는 부품에 관해 우주비행사들과 대화하는 장면을 소개하는 (C), Then(그런 다음)을 사용해 앞선 대화 이후 HAL-9000이 하는 일로 다음 단계에 대한 권고를 전한다는 것과 추가적으로 수행할 수 있는 일들을 소개한 뒤, 당시 영화에서만 볼 수 있었던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 2008년에 국제우주정거장에서 CIMON이라는 AI 로봇으로 현실화했다고 설명하는 (A), CIMON을 It(그것)으로 가리켜 그것이 우주선 내부를 돌아다닐 수 있는 공중에 떠다니는 구 모양의 로봇이라고 설명을 이어가는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies ⓐ[describing / described] in films are now a reality. One of them ⓑ[is / are] self-driving cars. (A) In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. (B) The taxi is capable of driving itself without any human intervention. (C) ⓒ[Had / Having] seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars. (D) Luckily, self-driving cars are being developed and certain versions are already on the road. (E)
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Additionally, many other AI technologies from movies are either in use or under development.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘게다가, 영화 속의 많은 다른 AI 기술이 사용되고 있거나 개발 중에 있습니다.’라는 뜻으로, Additionally(게다가)를 사용해 앞에서 설명한 AI 기술 외에 다른 기술들에 관한 내용을 덧붙이는 흐름이므로, 영화 <Total Recall>에 등장하는 자율주행 택시를 예로 들어 AI 기술을 통한 자율주행 자동차가 현재 개발되고 있고 특정 모델은 이미 도로에서 운행되고 있다고 설명한 뒤인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies ⓐ[describing / described] in films are now a reality. One of them ⓑ[is / are] self-driving cars. (A) In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. (B) The taxi is capable of driving itself without any human intervention. (C) ⓒ[Had / Having] seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars. (D) Luckily, self-driving cars are being developed and certain versions are already on the road. (E)
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: described is Had
describing is Had
described are Having
describing are Having
described is Having
solution:
ⓐ 수식을 받는 앞의 명사구(Several ~ technologies)가 영화에서 ‘묘사되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 described가 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘One of+복수명사(구)’ 형태가 주어일 때 동사는 핵심단어인 One에 수를 일치시키므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(many people wanted self-driving cars) 앞에 동사구가 놓일 수 없으므로 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사구문을 이루어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 many people이 ‘본’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 that movie가 있으며, 흐름상 주절 동사(wanted)가 나타내는 과거 시점 이전에 일어난 일에 해당하므로, 완료형 분사구문(Having+p.p. ~)을 이루는 Having이 알맞다.

오답
ⓐ 주어 Some AI programs가 타동사 refine(~을 개선하다)의 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으며, 흐름상 과거부터 현재까지 ‘개선되어 왔다’라는 의미를 나타내야 하므로, 복수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 복수형 조동사를 사용한 현재완료 수동태(have+been+p.p.)인 have been refined는 알맞다.
